# M13 (SPEC) — BUNKER CHAT GATEWAYS
Status: DESIGN AUTHORITY for the bunker chat-gateway capability. This file is the spec the implementation waves build from; the rendered handbook chapter (also `M13-chat-gateways.md`, same slug) is added by the render row, not by this file.
Owner directive (verbatim, 2026-11-22): "Update specs and boardctl so that each bunker Hermes can also be in telegram correctly so it's not just a scheduler routing but telegram and other chat gateway options".

## 1. Purpose
Today a bunker Hermes has no chat presence: it receives work through Crier and the scheduler, and its reports surface only through the control host's scheduler routing. This spec gives every bunker Hermes its own chat-gateway connections — Telegram first, gateway-platform agnostic — so a bunker can (a) hold a chat identity of its own, (b) deliver tick reports directly into configured chat threads, and (c) remain fully operable when chat is absent.

## 2. Law (normative statements)
- **R1 — Per-bunker gateway identity.** Each bunker Hermes MAY run its own gateway connections (`platforms.*` in its `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, mirroring the control host's verified surface: `platforms.telegram.{enabled, home_channel{platform, chat_id, name, thread_id, user_id}}`). Each bunker uses its OWN bot token — never the control host's token. check: two bunkers configured with distinct tokens answer to distinct bot identities. - **R2 — Token custody is by reference.** Tokens are referenced, never inlined: the generated config names an env var or secret file (`token_env: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`), and generated files on disk contain zero token bytes. check: `grep -rEo '[0-9]{8,10}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35}'` over a provisioned bunker home returns nothing while the gateway is live. - **R3 — Scheduler routing and chat delivery are independent.** A bunker with no gateways configured remains a fully valid lane (scheduler-only). Chat delivery never gates task acceptance; the Crier boundary (M10) is unchanged. check: a bunker lane with empty `platforms` completes ticks and delivers to the scheduler exactly as today. - **R4 — Report law is identical on bunkers.** When a bunker lane carries a delivery target (`deliver: telegram:<chat_id>:<thread_id>` in the scheduler project row), every tick attempt delivers its report link to that thread — success or failure — exactly as control-host lanes do (M9 deliver law). - **R5 — Gateway-platform agnostic.** The config schema and provisioning code must accept any platform key the control-host Hermes accepts (`telegram`, `signal`, `discord`, …) without bunker-side special-casing. Telegram is the first proven platform, not a schema constant. check: a config with `platforms.signal.enabled: true` provisions without error even before any signal gateway is exercised. - **R6 — Fail fast on dead credentials.** An invalid or revoked token must fail the gateway within seconds with a named error in the bunker's own log — never a silent hang that stalls ticks. check: revoked-token probe logs an auth error and the lane's tick latency is unchanged.

## 3. Config surface (exact)
Generated/merged into each bunker's `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (same keys the control host uses; verified against the local Hermes config surface 2026-11-22):
```yaml platforms: telegram: enabled: true token_env: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN # R2: reference, not a token home_channel: platform: telegram chat_id: "<chat_id>" thread_id: "<thread_id>" name: "<chat name>" allowed_chats: ["<chat_id>"] gateways: loop_watchdog: {} # inherit Hermes defaults; bunkers may override ```
Scheduler project row (control host, already supported): `deliver = "telegram:<chat>:<thread>"`, `deliver_mode = "link"` (owner ruling 2026-11-16: link mode, into this thread).

## 4. Wiring
- **Provisioning:** `scripts/bunker_config_gen.py` gains a `gateways` input section; it emits the §3 block with `token_env` references and merges it into the bunker config at provision and re-sync; `scripts/verify-node.sh` gains a gateway leg (config parses; no token bytes on disk; `token_env` var resolves on the bunker). - **boardctl:** rows carry optional delivery metadata so closeout tooling can route evidence without chat-specific knowledge: `boardctl create --deliver telegram:<chat>:<thread>` (`--deliver-mode link|full`), stored as row keys `deliver` / `deliver_mode`; read back by `boardctl show`. The board stays platform-agnostic — the field is a routing hint, not a delivery engine. - **Scheduler:** no schema change (deliver/deliver_mode already exist). The bunker lane profile documentation (M9/M13) records the deliver law for bunker lanes. - **Secrets:** bunker tokens live in each bunker's own env/secret store; provisioning copies only the REFERENCE. The control host never holds bunker bot tokens.

## 5. Error catalog
| Condition | Behavior | |---|---| | token missing on bunker | gateway disabled at startup, lane runs scheduler-only, provisioning reports `GATEWAY_TOKEN_REF_UNRESOLVED` (warning, not fatal) | | token invalid/revoked | gateway auth error within seconds (R6), tick pipeline unaffected | | chat delivery fails (network/platform) | report delivery retries per Hermes gateway defaults; tick completion is NOT blocked (R3) | | disallowed chat attempts command | Hermes `allowed_chats` enforcement (control-host behavior), no bunker-specific path |

## 6. Out of scope (explicit)
- Bunker-to-bunker chat, group-chat moderation, media ingestion on bunkers. - Any change to Crier transport or task-acceptance semantics (M10 stays authoritative). - Making chat delivery a dependency of any gate or judge.

## 7. Acceptance checks (runnable)
1. `python3 scripts/bunker_config_gen.py --check --config <cfg>` exits 0 on a config with a `gateways` section and prints the emitted platform keys. 2. `grep -rEo '[0-9]{8,10}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35}' <bunker_home>` returns no matches while the gateway is configured (R2). 3. `boardctl create --deliver telegram:-1003310984808:196286 …` then `boardctl show <id>` prints the `deliver` value (boardctl row). 4. `python3 scripts/handbook_lint.py` → `handbook_lint: clean` after the render row adds the chapter to BOOK.yaml with its register syncs. 5. A bunker lane tick completes with gateways disabled and delivers to the scheduler (R3).
